clues.text: This town sits on a big river in the flat grass lands of its state. Farms and fields spread out on all sides.
clues.narrowing: Points to a prairie-region city on a river in the deep south.

source.quote: The city sits on the Pearl River and is located in the greater Jackson Prairie region of Mississippi.

clues.text: Bad storms hit this town a lot, with big hail, wild winds, and twisters. Snow is rare and soon melts.
clues.narrowing: Keeps storm-prone southern capitals where snow almost never lasts.

source.quote: Jackson lies in a region prone to severe thunderstorms which can produce large hail, damaging winds, and tornadoes.

clues.text: Long ago, a trade post stood on a bluff by the river. The state picked that bluff as the site for its new capital town.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to the bluff chosen as the new state's capital site in 1821.

source.quote: LeFleur's Bluff was developed when it was chosen as the site for the new state's capital city.

clues.text: Deep down under this town sleeps a dead volcano. Its peak lies far below the streets, right under a sports hall.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: only one capital city sits atop a buried volcano.

source.quote: Jackson sits atop the extinct Jackson Volcano, located 2,900 feet (880 m) underground.

clues.text: The governor of Mississippi works in this city, the largest in the state. Lawmakers meet here to make the state's laws.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and lawmakers of Mississippi work in this city.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Mississippi

reveal.blurb: Founded in 1821 as the new state capital, this river city was named for a general who later became president. Union troops burned it three times in the Civil War, leaving only chimneys standing. Jackson is the capital of Mississippi.
